source.title: Towards Multi-Fidelity Scaling Laws of Neural Surrogates in CFD
source.authors: Paul Setinek; Gianluca Galletti; J. Brandstetter

page_placements.theme: Multi-fidelity simulation allocation depends on target and fidelity gap

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to CFD neural surrogates and reports performance results under varying dataset-generation budgets and fidelity mixtures. It does not fit or verify a power-law form.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MSE trends for Transolver models evaluated on 120 unseen high-fidelity samples. The figures show the results, while the text describes their direction and the transfer patterns. It does not report fitted power-law exponents, predictions from small runs, or parameter/token scaling.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments vary the data-generation budget (a data axis) for a fixed ~4M-parameter Transolver on CFD and report how MSE changes, so they bear on V5 in a new setting. The paper gives no power-law fit, exponent or numeric values; it only states that error falls as budget rises. The power-law form V5 names therefore cannot be checked, and no verdict is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors claim a 'clear trend' of error decreasing with data-generation budget, which they call analogous to classical scaling laws but do not fit. They call the work an initial step, with optimal fidelity mixes that depend on budget and limited transfer when the fidelity gap is large.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies CFD simulation-data generation budget and low-/high-fidelity composition for a fixed-size neural operator; it does not reproduce language-model loss scaling or fit the original scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed composition effect varies by output field: pressure and volumetric velocity show positive transfer from low-fidelity data at lower budgets, whereas wall shear stress does not. The preferred composition also shifts with data-generation budget.

fits_no_version.finding: For pressure and volumetric velocity, low/high-fidelity mixtures beat all-high-fidelity data at low budgets, and the optimal mix shifts toward low fidelity as the budget shrinks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a fixed simulation budget, the error-minimising mix of low- and high-fidelity training data depends on the budget.

fits_no_version.finding: For wall shear stress, there is no positive transfer from low-fidelity data at any budget. The authors link this to a large fidelity gap (nMAE 0.405/0.796 vs 0.04 for pressure, Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether low-fidelity data transfers positively depends on the per-field discrepancy between fidelities.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at the AI for Science workshop (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: Only one neural-operator architecture at a fixed size (∼4M parameters) is studied. The paper reports MSE trends in figures but gives no numerical MSE values or fitted power-law exponents, so the claimed shape of a scaling law cannot be assessed. Experiments average four seeds and use 120 high-fidelity test samples.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported field results were omitted.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss; no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute; no fit.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No parameter/token allocation versus compute. The 'compute-optimal' framing concerns the fidelity mix under a simulation budget at fixed model size.
Power-law form of MSE versus data-generation budget: no fit, exponent or orders-of-magnitude range. The budget spans only about 1000-6600 core hours. Model size and training compute are not varied.
No comparison of fitting choices and no analysis of curvature.

missing.what: Per-field nMAE between low- and high-fidelity simulations (pressure about 0.04; WSS x 0.405, y 0.796; velocity 0.118/0.303), used to explain the transfer pattern

record.verdict_notes: The paper is framed as 'scaling laws', but it fixes model size and reports no power-law fits. Its evidence on V5 amounts to monotone improvement with data budget over less than one order of magnitude. For that reason no supports or limits_scope label is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out cross-entropy sweep over parameters, tokens, or training compute, and no power-law fit.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
The study varies data-generation budget and low-/high-fidelity composition, not the parameter and token allocation or its growth with training compute.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.

The study examines CFD surrogate performance as data-generation budget and fidelity composition vary, but does not fit or test whether the results follow the same power-law form. It does not examine image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes beyond its low-/high-fidelity dataset setting.
No downstream-task performance or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents, and no analysis of curves bending away from a power law.

relation.reason: The study reports its own budget-scaling experiments rather than merely citing or assuming scaling behavior.

tranche.reason: The fixed-size CFD neural surrogate experiments examine error versus data-generation budget in a new setting relevant to V5, although they do not establish a power-law form.

source_check.notes: No power-law fit or exponent is reported; cannot_determine is appropriate for V5. Table 2 gives surface WSS nMAEs of 0.405/0.796; pressure nMAE is 0.040 in volume and 0.043 on the surface.
